Timeline::strftime¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline::strftime(std::string_view fmt) -> Note

What It Does¶

Formats every timestamp in the timeline into text using a strftime-style format string.

This is the main bridge from temporal data into labels, report text, export strings, and human-facing calendar representations.

Parameters¶

fmt

The format string to apply to each timestamp.

Common directives include:

  • %Y Four-digit year.

  • %m Zero-padded month number.

  • %d Zero-padded day of month.

  • %H Zero-padded hour.

  • %M Zero-padded minute.

  • %S Zero-padded second.

  • %f Fractional seconds.

  • %z Numeric timezone offset.

  • %a Abbreviated weekday name.

  • %A Full weekday name.

  • %b Abbreviated month name.

  • %B Full month name.

Returns¶

Note A text object with the same shape as the input timeline.

Examples¶

Example 1. Build compact report labels with year, month, day, hour, and minute.

auto out = base.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M");
std::cout << pluss::note::print(out) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["2024-11-01 09:00", "2024-11-01 10:15", "2024-12-31 23:59", "2025-01-01 00:00"]

Example 2. Switch the format string to produce weekday and abbreviated month labels instead.

auto out = base.strftime("%A, %b %d");
std::cout << pluss::note::print(out) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["Friday, Nov 01", "Friday, Nov 01", "Tuesday, Dec 31", "Wednesday, Jan 01"]

Notes¶

  • strftime() is the flexible formatting surface.

  • If you always want canonical ISO output, to_note_iso is shorter and more explicit.

  • The output lives in Note, so it naturally composes with the text-processing surfaces in PlussQit and PlussAI.
